page: Microsoft Azure D64a_v4 is a general-purpose virtual machine based on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The instance features 64 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 32 physical cores of an AMD EPYC 7452 processor operating at up to 3.35 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. Hardware features include support for AVX, AES, and SHA-NI cryptographic extensions, while excluding AVX-512 and AMX instruction sets. Memory is provisioned at 256 GB of RAM, yielding a balanced 4:1 memory-to-vCPU allocation ratio. Local storage consists of a bundled 1718 GB SSD, and no discrete GPUs or complimentary public IPv4 addresses are included.

Benchmark results highlight strong parallel throughput alongside modest single-core execution speed. Single-core tests such as stress-ng register in the lower 10th percentile, and Geekbench single-core reaches an average rating of 1610.0. In contrast, multi-threaded workloads demonstrate solid scaling, indicated by a Geekbench multi-core score of 17263.0, PassMark CPU of 63075.82, and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression reaching 298.78 GB/sec. Memory subsystems demonstrate high throughput, achieving a top-tier PassMark memory score of 3066.82 and cached read bandwidth of 4168.16 GB/sec.

The 64 vCPU scale and 256 GB RAM capacity offer effective resource density for memory-sensitive enterprise systems that distribute load evenly across many cores. The presence of 1718 GB of fast local SSD storage reduces dependence on external disks for intermediate files and temporary scratchpads. However, applications dependent on ultra-fast single-threaded response or AVX-512 vectorization will encounter performance ceilings.

This hardware footprint fits multi-threaded backend workloads, including relational database operations, in-memory caching layers like Redis, build pipelines, enterprise data transformation, and CPU-based inference pipelines for lightweight machine learning models.
description: Microsoft Azure D64a_v4 is a general-purpose virtual machine equipped with 64 dedicated vCPUs and 256 GB of system memory, driven by a 32-core AMD EPYC 7452 processor running at 3.35 GHz. Built on Microsoft Hyper-V, the system incorporates an x86_64 architecture with AES and SHA instruction sets, omitting AVX-512 extensions and discrete GPUs. Storage is addressed locally by a bundled 1718 GB SSD. Benchmark metrics highlight strong multi-core processing, exceptional memory performance scoring in the top 10 percent on PassMark, and 298.78 GB/sec multi-threaded decompression, despite modest single-thread CPU benchmarks. The standard 4:1 memory-to-core ratio combined with sizeable NVMe-backed local storage makes this instance suitable for parallel computational tasks, database workloads, large batch processing, and high-concurrency web services.
